value: Many large K-12 school districts are banning OpenAI's ChatGPT over concerns about cheating and plagiarism, as teachers fear it bypasses traditional detection. However, education technology experts advocate against outright bans, arguing that AI is an unavoidable part of students' future and should instead be integrated through teacher and student training. They contend bans are ineffective, urging schools to improve assessment design and teach ethical AI use. OpenAI, for its part, is developing detection tools. While some districts implement bans, colleges largely opt for policy guidance over prohibition, reflecting a varied institutional response to this emerging technology.
